verdict.gold_reason: Article 22(1)(i) of Regulation 2017/1485 lists curtailment of already allocated cross-zonal capacity as a remedial action. It requires an emergency where using the capacity endangers operational security, agreement of all TSOs at the given interconnector, and that re-dispatching or countertrading is not possible. The reference answer matches this text.

other_articles.why: Art 72(1) allows curtailment in force majeure or emergency when redispatching or countertrading is not possible, and requires coordination with all directly concerned TSOs. It does not list this as a remedial action and does not use the 'agree' wording.
Art 16(2) limits transaction curtailment to emergencies where redispatching or countertrading is not possible. It adds no condition about agreement among TSOs.

verdict.ambiguity_reason: The wording 'one of its grid-security countermeasures' points to the remedial-actions list, which is Art 22. Art 72 of Reg 2015/1222 could be read as an alternative, but it gives a different further condition (coordination or liaison) rather than agreement.
